title: OSS-708 reads a key prefix anywhere in a diff, so random base64 fails the gate as a GitHub token
foundBy: session agent, when campaign's `make ci` failed OSS-708 on a re-recorded cassette
details:
Campaign's `make ci` failed OSS-708 with `a GitHub token is in 1 commit(s)`. The match was `ghs_` and 47 more characters in the middle of a Codex `encrypted_content` field. That field is reasoning ciphertext in base64, and the characters before the prefix were `9C`. It was not a token.

The history scan confirms each probe with a pattern that has no word boundary in front, so a key prefix counts anywhere in a diff. The tree scan anchors the same patterns with `\b`, and passes the same file. Base64 turns up every prefix by chance, and a recorded model turn carries kilobytes of it. A repository that commits recordings meets this again at random, and the only way through is to rewrite its history.
